summary: Concrete, fast execution with numbers and owners. Little about why decisions are fair, or about people after a setback. Written English is clear but simpler than the certificate suggests.

questions.question: Your robot broke two days before the final. How was the team feeling, and what did you do for them — not only for the robot?
questions.why: The setback story is about fixing the machine; how the team came through is missing.

evidence.quote: We rebuilt the arm overnight and still made it.

questions.question: What was the riskiest decision in the clean-up or the final, and what could it have cost?
questions.why: No answer weighs a risk or its consequences.

questions.question: Why do real bus times matter to the people who would use the app — and who might it leave out?
questions.why: The idea is clear; the thinking about its users is not.

evidence.quote: I want to make an app that shows real bus times.

questions.question: Tell me about a time doing the right thing slowed you down. What did you choose, and why?
questions.why: No answer touches values or fairness.

questions.question: Walk me through the clean-up: who chose the streets and the leaders, and what would you change?
questions.why: Strong execution evidence — confirm the plan was their own.

evidence.quote: Each team had a leader and a list of streets.

flags.title: How they make decisions
flags.ask: Ask for a recent decision and exactly how it was made.

sources.quote: I always ask everyone's opinion before I decide anything.
I prefer to decide quickly and explain my reasons later.

clarify.topic: Their own part in the robotics result, apart from the team’s.

evidence.quote: I led our robotics team to the regional final

clarify.topic: What else changed after the setback, beyond spare parts.

evidence.quote: I learned to always have spare parts.

english.basis: Short sentences and a narrow range of vocabulary in the written answers; almost no errors.
